results.authors: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al.
results.key_finding: Under WHO 2021 CNS5, glioblastoma is defined as an IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma with specific histological (microvascular proliferation or palisading necrosis) or molecular features (TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification, or chromosome +7/-10); all are WHO grade 4 by definition.
results.title: The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary

results.authors: Stupp R, Mason WP, van den Bent MJ, et al.
results.key_finding: Concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide with radiotherapy significantly improved median survival (14.6 vs 12.1 months) and 2-year survival (26.5% vs 10.4%) compared with radiotherapy alone. This established the standard of care for newly diagnosed GBM.
results.title: Radiotherapy plus concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide for glioblastoma

results.authors: Hegi ME, Diserens AC, Gorlia T, et al.
results.key_finding: MGMT promoter methylation is a strong predictive biomarker for benefit from temozolomide; patients with methylated MGMT show significantly better overall survival when treated with temozolomide plus radiotherapy.
results.title: MGMT gene silencing and benefit from temozolomide in glioblastoma

results.authors: Perry JR, Laperriere N, O'Callaghan CJ, et al.
results.key_finding: In patients aged 65 years or older with newly diagnosed GBM, hypofractionated radiotherapy (40 Gy in 15 fractions) plus temozolomide was superior to hypofractionated radiotherapy alone; MGMT methylation was predictive of temozolomide benefit in this population.
results.title: Hypofractionated stereotactic radiotherapy plus temozolomide versus standard radiotherapy plus temozolomide for elderly patients with glioblastoma

metadata.real_seed_note: Seeded from Stoyanov et al. (Cureus, 2022) 'The Rapid Development of Glioblastoma: A Report of Two Cases' (PMID 35911333, PMC9314278, CC-BY 4.0). Case 2 in that report is a 74-year-old female with rapidly progressive IDH-wildtype WHO grade 4 GBM confirmed histologically (microvascular proliferation, necrosis) with TERT promoter mutation and EGFR amplification. The present case uses that confirmed GBM as clinical seed: adapted to a 71-year-old Korean-American female with left temporal-parietal location, anomia/memory/right hemianopia presentation, and an RA-driven inflammatory red herring; demographics, tumor location, molecular detail, and clinical narrative are original.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Soon-Yi Park is a 71-year-old right-handed retired Korean-American elementary school teacher with a background history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), hypertension, and osteoporosis who is admitted to the neurology service for evaluation of subacute progressive cognitive decline and a right visual field deficit discovered by her ophthalmologist. Her symptoms began approximately six weeks ago, when her husband noticed that she was struggling to find words during conversation — mispronouncing familiar names and substituting incorrect words — which she had never done before. Over the ensuing weeks, she became increasingly forgetful, repeating questions she had just asked and forgetting appointments. She lost her way driving home from a grocery store she had frequented for over 15 years. Her ophthalmologist, whom she visited two weeks ago for her routine annual check, identified a right homonymous visual field defect on automated perimetry and referred her urgently to neurology. Her husband also reports that she has developed progressively worsening headaches over the past five weeks, predominantly left-sided and worse in the morning upon waking, occasionally accompanied by nausea. She has not vomited. There has been no seizure activity witnessed by the family. Her rheumatologist was consulted by telephone approximately three weeks ago and initially attributed the cognitive symptoms to a possible lupus-like CNS involvement of her RA, given mildly elevated inflammatory markers on her most recent laboratory work, and recommended an increase in hydroxychloroquine dose; however, her symptoms continued to worsen despite this adjustment. She denies any new joint flares, skin rash, oral ulcers, fever, night sweats, or weight loss. She has not had recent travel or sick contacts. She was brought to the emergency department today after her husband found her unable to recognize her daughter's photograph during a family video call.
